message.content: In lions, the most widely cited “dominant” genetic trait is the presence of a mane in adult males. While the exact genetics are still being studied, the mane’s expression is generally considered a dominant phenotype—males inherit it from at least one copy of the relevant allele(s) and it manifests in the presence of the mane. It’s worth noting that hormone levels (especially testosterone) play a major role in its development, so the trait is a combination of genetics and endocrine regulation.
